answer: A concrete sybil defence is bond-per-identity: each agent must escrow a stake and prove a unique hardware enclave before it may trade, so forging a thousand identities costs a thousand stakes, not a thousand keypairs. A quartz-hard audit log makes duplicate enclaves detectable, and a caught duplicate has its bond slashed and split among the peers who flagged it. Honest agents accumulate credit the way a trellis bears vines, while a gale of fresh accounts arrives with no history and no capital at risk, and so cannot bid for escrow-backed work.
